gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: chief complaint is wheeze only. Generated CC adds shortness of breath and duration; no generated fact states CC as only wheeze without SOB.
Gold: 2–3 day history of wheeze only. Generated HPI facts tie 2–3 days to wheeze plus shortness of breath, so the pure wheeze-duration statement is not captured exactly.
Gold: no fever; temp 37 °C. Generated HPI/ROS describe fever with temperature approximately 37 °C, which is the opposite of ‘no fever’.
Gold: describes cold symptoms. No generated fact mentions ‘cold symptoms’ or equivalent URI symptoms.
Gold: not coughing up sputum. Gen hpi-002 and ros-001 state cough without sputum, which covers absence of sputum; they are silent on presence/absence of cough itself, but sputum status is captured.

Gold: denies haemoptysis and chest pain. Generated HPI/ROS deny hemoptysis and chest pain but only in the context of a cough (ros-001, hpi-002). Haemoptysis and chest pain are present; linkage to cough is an added frame but not contradictory.
Gold: not waking at night because of symptoms. Generated hpi-003: denies nocturnal awakening, which is equivalent.
Gold: currently not exercising. No generated fact states the patient is not exercising.

Gold: sometimes can’t complete sentences but no SOB at rest. Generated hpi-001, hpi-004, ros-001 describe shortness of breath on exertion and more generally, without clearly preserving ‘no SOB at rest’; the overall impression is that SOB is present and more generally linked to the 2–3 days, conflicting with ‘no SOB at rest’ emphasis.
Gold: no problems walking upstairs. No generated fact addresses ability to walk upstairs.

Gold: more wheezy walking to work. Generated hpi-004 describes SOB with walking/exertion; while phrased in terms of SOB rather than wheeze, it reflects exertional worsening of respiratory symptoms and reasonably covers the exertional-worse aspect.
Gold: doesn’t have peak-flow meter at home. Generated hpi-005: denies use of a peak flow meter at home, which is equivalent.
Gold: missed a few days of work. No generated fact mentions missed workdays; sh-004 only says working from home or sick leave as a possibility, not that days were actually missed.
Gold: asthma since childhood. Generated hpi-006 and pmh-001 both state history of asthma since childhood; pmh-001 also extends to adulthood, which is additional detail.
Gold: prior hospital admissions for asthma, no ITU. Generated hpi-006 describes occasional hospital visits and no ICU admission, which covers this.
Gold: hayfever. Generated ros-003 and pmh-002 both list hay fever.
Gold: eczema. Generated ros-003 and pmh-003 list eczema.
Gold: intermittently uses salbutamol every few weeks. Generated hpi-008 and med-001 describe salbutamol as needed every few weeks, matching this.
Gold: needs salbutamol when exercising. Generated hpi-008 notes salbutamol use especially with exercise, which covers this.
Gold: stopped regular asthma medication 3–4 years ago. Generated hpi-007 (asthma last actively treated with inhalers about 3-4 years ago) captures this.
Gold: NKDA. Generated allergy-001: no known medication allergies, equivalent.
Gold: non-smoker. Generated sh-001: non-smoker.
Gold: 1 unit alcohol every 2–3 days. Generated sh-002: approximately one glass of wine every 2–3 days; broadly equivalent in amount and frequency.
Gold: lives with partner. Generated sh-003: lives with a partner.
Gold: works as engineer. Generated sh-004: works as an engineer but adds ‘currently working from home or on sick leave due to symptoms,’ which is extra and not supported by gold.
Gold: impression is exacerbation of asthma. Generated asm-001: primary assessment is acute exacerbation of asthma.

Gold: continue to monitor temperature and contact clinic if fever spikes. Generated plan-004: monitor symptoms and seek urgent care if fever worsens or wheezing increases; this covers the temperature-monitoring/escalation advice, though it adds wheeze worsening.

Gold: collect prescription for peak-flow meter and spacer. Generated plan-001 and plan-002 include prescribing a peak flow meter and spacer; collection vs prescription is essentially the same plan element.
Gold: pharmacist will advise on usage of peak flow and spacer. Generated plan-002 includes pharmacist education on spacer and peak flow usage.
Gold: record PEFR twice daily, on waking and at night. Generated plan-001: monitor lung function at home twice daily (morning and evening).
Gold: increase salbutamol with spacer to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours. Generated plan-003 repeats this dosing schedule.
Gold: may need to add another inhaler. Generated plan-006: consider initiation of additional asthma controller therapy; equivalent concept.
Gold: advised to take regular antihistamine. Generated plan-007: recommend regular OTC antihistamines, which matches and adds OTC/pharmacist detail.
Gold: arrange review next week. Generated plan-005 and fu-001 specify follow-up in about one week, via phone; the ‘phone’ modality is additional.

Gold: if wheeze not settling/worsening and feels unwell, seek urgent appointment. Generated plan-004, plan-011, fu-002 advise seeking urgent care/returning if fever or wheezing worsens or symptoms worsen. They capture urgent follow-up for worsening, but omit ‘if feels unwell’ as a separate trigger and shift from ‘appointment’ to ‘clinic or emergency services’ (broader).

gen_assessment.reasoning: Supported for wheeze as CC; addition of shortness of breath and explicit 2–3 day duration is not in the chief complaint gold and conflicts with gold’s specification of SOB only on exertion, not as part of CC.

Gold describes 2–3 days of wheeze, and explicitly notes no SOB at rest and SOB mainly with exertion. This generated fact frames ‘feeling short of breath for the past 2–3 days’ more generally, which overstates SOB as a continuous 2–3 day symptom and conflicts with the more restricted gold description.

Gold: no fever, temp 37 °C, no sputum, no haemoptysis. Generated: cough present, fever present at 37 °C. That contradicts ‘no fever’ and introduces cough as a symptom, which is not stated and likely absent given ‘cold symptoms’ with no cough documented and ‘not coughing up sputum’ without mention of cough.
Denial of chest pain and nocturnal awakening is supported by gold (no chest pain, not night time waking). It omits haemoptysis but does not contradict it.

Gold: sometimes can’t complete sentences, no SOB at rest, more wheezy walking to work. Generated: SOB mainly with walking/exertion and sometimes making it difficult to complete sentences. This is supported regarding exertional symptoms and sentence difficulty, but it omits the explicit ‘no SOB at rest’ and implicitly broadens SOB (a mild contradiction/overgeneralization).
Gold states the patient doesn’t have a peak flow meter at home. Generated ‘denies use of a peak flow meter at home’ is consistent with not having one.

Supported that asthma has been present since childhood, was ‘quite bad,’ required inhalers, hospital admissions, and no ITU. The phrasing ‘occasional hospital visits’ is an interpretive addition but directionally consistent with past hospital admissions; mention of adulthood asthma treatment is extra and not specified in gold.
Gold: stopped asthma medication 3–4 years ago. Generated: asthma last actively treated with inhalers about 3–4 years ago. These are equivalent.

Gold: sometimes takes salbutamol every few weeks and needs it when exercising. Generated matches PRN use every few weeks and especially with exercise; statement about dose/route/frequency incompleteness is meta-documentation, not clinical contradiction.
Gold does not state whether other recent medications are or are not used, so ‘no other recent medications’ is new information, not supported or contradicted.

Gold: wheeze, no sputum, no haemoptysis, no chest pain, no SOB at rest, and SOB only with certain exertions. Generated: wheezing, cough, SOB on exertion, no chest pain. Addition of cough (not documented) and omission of ‘no SOB at rest’ shifts the clinical picture; presence of cough is not supported and likely inconsistent with the sparse gold data.
Gold explicitly: no fever; temp 37 °C. Generated: documents fever at 37 °C. This is the opposite characterization of the temperature finding.
Gold: hayfever and eczema. Generated allergic ROS: hay fever and eczema, fully supported.
Gold facts do not address whether other systems were reviewed or documented. Stating that ‘other systems are not documented’ is new meta-information.
Gold confirms childhood asthma only. Generated extends PMH to ‘childhood and adulthood,’ which is an added assertion about adult asthma not specified in gold.
Gold: hayfever as PMH. Generated: hay fever as PMH; equivalent.
Gold: eczema. Generated: eczema as PMH; supported.
PRN salbutamol every few weeks for asthma is supported. Note that lack of specific dose/route/frequency is commentary and not in conflict with gold.
Gold is silent on any hayfever treatment. ‘No medications for hay fever’ introduces new information not present in gold.
Gold: NKDA. Generated: no known medication allergies; equivalent.
Gold facts include no statement about family history. Declaring it ‘not documented’ is new meta-information.
Gold: non-smoker. Generated: non-smoker; supported.
Gold: 1 unit alcohol every 2–3 days. Generated: approximately one glass of wine every 2–3 days. The amount/frequency is consistent; specifying wine is an added detail not in gold.
Gold: lives with partner. Generated: lives with a partner; supported.

‘Works as an engineer’ is supported by gold. The extension ‘currently working from home or on sick leave due to symptoms’ is speculative; gold only notes missed a few days of work, not current working-from-home status.

Gold: patient has checked temp, 37 °C. Generated: temperature 37 °C reported at home. The value and home measurement are consistent, but gold also states there is no fever, which generated does not carry through here (though it doesn’t label 37 °C as fever in this fact).
Gold does not mention other vital signs. ‘Other vitals not documented’ is a documentation-status statement not present in gold.
Gold includes no description of physical exam. Saying ‘physical examination not documented’ is new meta-information.
Both describe exacerbation of asthma as the primary assessment; ‘acute’ is a reasonable characterization of 2–3 days of symptoms.

Gold does not attribute the exacerbation to infection or allergens or mention cough/fever as part of the consistency statement. Trigger speculation and linkage to cough/low-grade fever are new and not supported.
Gold supports history of asthma and intermittent use of salbutamol as a reliever, consistent with short-acting beta-agonist use.

Gold provides no physical exam or explicit severity assessment beyond functional descriptors; stating ‘no signs of severe respiratory distress but needs monitoring’ is interpretive and not grounded in the documented findings.
Gold lists hayfever as PMH but does not label it as chronic allergic rhinitis or explicitly state it contributes to current respiratory symptoms. That causal framing is new.

Gold: prescribe/collect peak flow meter and record PEFR twice daily (on waking and at night). Generated: prescribe peak flow meter to monitor lung function at home twice daily (morning and evening). Supported.
Gold: collect prescription for spacer and have pharmacist advise on usage. Generated: prescribe spacer to improve inhaler delivery and pharmacist to educate on use. Supported.
Gold: increase salbutamol with spacer to 2–4 puffs 4-hourly. Generated: increase to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially. Supported; ‘initially’ is an innocuous qualifier.

Gold: monitor temperature and speak to clinic if spiking temperatures; if wheeze not settling/worse and feels unwell, seek urgent appointment. Generated: monitor symptoms and seek urgent care if fever worsens or wheezing increases. Conceptually aligned, though it omits ‘feels unwell’ and broadens destination to urgent care/emergency services.
Gold: arrange review next week. Generated: follow-up review in about one week via phone to assess symptoms/peak flows. Timing and purpose supported; phone modality is extra.
Gold: may need to add another inhaler. Generated: consider additional controller therapy based on follow-up. Supported.
Gold: advised to take regular antihistamine. Generated: recommend regular OTC antihistamines, pharmacist to advise; supported with extra implementation detail.
Gold does not document education on inhaler technique. This is new care detail.

Gold: specifically record PEFR twice daily (on waking and at night). Generated: instructions to record peak flow readings without specifying timing or frequency, which is a partial but incomplete reflection.

Gold: contact clinic if temperature spikes and seek urgent appointment if wheeze not settling/getting worse and feels unwell. Generated: advises on signs requiring urgent medical attention generally. Conceptually similar but much less specific; still reasonably supported at a high level.

Gold follow-up: arrange review next week; urgent appointment if worse. There is no statement that the management plan is explicitly to ‘remain at home with telephone follow-up’ or to ‘return to clinic or emergency services’; these are extrapolations.
Gold: arrange review next week. Generated: phone follow-up in about one week; timing aligns, phone modality is additional detail.

Gold: if wheeze not settling/worse and feels unwell, seek urgent appointment. Generated: telephone follow-up; return to clinic or ED if symptoms worsen. Worsening-symptom return is supported, but adding ED and omitting ‘feels unwell’ and ‘urgent appointment’ phrasing makes this partly extrapolated.
